# Assembled 14 September 2026. *** DELIBERATELY NOT MERGED. *** This archive conflated two Arturo
# Lerenas earlier in the same week and had to retract a whole branch within the hour; the discipline
# that came out of that is applied here.

Godmother at the Catedral de Montevideo

column3: *** "LERENA de L[erena], JOSEFA, m, 43, VIUDA, R. Oriental" *** - born about 1852. On the lines above, the same enumerator writes married women as [maiden surname] + "de L.", so if he is consistent she was BORN A LERENA AND MARRIED A LERENA

column1: Death at Montevideo
column3: *** "JOSEFA LORENA LERENA TRAIBEL", aged 96, born 1851. Parents: AVELINO LERENA and AMBROCIA TRAIBEL *** - which places the LERENA TRAIBEL branch this archive has named since its first week

column1: # *** WHAT FITS. *** The 1895 census gives her age as 43, implying birth about 1852; the death record
# says 1851. One year apart, which is nothing. Both are "R. Oriental" / Montevideo women. A woman who
# was in her brother-in-law's Buenos Aires house in 1895 and died at Montevideo in 1947 is entirely
# ordinary - the family crossed that river constantly.
# *** WHAT DOES NOT FIT, OR IS NOT TESTED. ***
# - The 1947 death record names NO SPOUSE. The census woman is a VIUDA. Neither contradicts the
#   other, but neither confirms it either.
# - The census form "Lerena de Lerena" would mean she married a man of her own surname. The death
#   record gives her as LERENA TRAIBEL - her parents' surnames, which is what a Uruguayan death record
#   gives whether or not she married.
# - *** NOTHING LINKS AVELINO LERENA TO SANCHO. *** An Avelino Lerena stood godfather at the Catedral
#   in 1833 to a child of Justa Pastora Lerena, Sancho's daughter - which is suggestive and no more.
#   Avelino's own parents are named in no record found here.
# *** SO: ONE STRONG CANDIDATE IDENTIFICATION, RECORDED AS THREE ROWS AND NOT MERGED. ***
# What would settle it: Josefa's MARRIAGE record. If she married a Lerena, the census reading is
# right and this family contains a LERENA-LERENA MARRIAGE one generation before Juan Carlos and
# Maria - which is the pattern the whole search turns on.
# ================ A FOURTH SIGHTING, AND IT WEAKENS MY OWN READING ================
# Added within the hour of publishing the paragraph above. 14 September 2026.
# *** THERE IS A JOSEFA LERENA WHO MARRIED FERNANDO MORATORIO. *** Uruguayan civil registration
# carries her as the mother of JOSEFA, EDUARDO and MARIA MORATORIO LERENA, with "Spouses: Fernando
# Moratorio". And FamilySearch's TREE attaches that woman to profile K4VN-52H - "Josefa Lerena
# Traibel, 1851-1947" - the same person as the 1947 death record above.
# *** SO THE CENSUS READING "LERENA DE LERENA" IS NO LONGER SAFE, and I published it an hour ago as
# the sharpest question in the project. ***
# WHAT THE IMAGE ACTUALLY SHOWS, re-examined at DeepZoom level 13 after this turned up: line 4 does
# read "Lerena de L. Josefa", and the "de L." is formed identically to lines 2 and 3. That part was
# read correctly. *** IT IS THE INFERENCE THAT WAS TOO CONFIDENT. *** "de L." can mean:
#   (a) she married a LERENA - what I argued; or
#   (b) the enumerator used "de L." as shorthand for THIS HOUSEHOLD, the Lerena house, and wrote it
#       against every married woman in it regardless of her husband's actual surname. Lines 2 and 3
#       are genuinely "de Lerena", so both readings fit them equally and neither tests the shorthand.
# If the census Josefa IS Josefa Lerena Traibel, then (b) is right and she was "de Moratorio".
# If she is a DIFFERENT Josefa, (a) may still stand - and there would then be two Josefa Lerenas of
# almost the same age, which is exactly the trap this file was written to avoid.
# *** THE TIERING, STATED PLAINLY. *** The Moratorio marriage records are INDEX-LEVEL civil
# registration - real records, not a tree. The link from that Josefa to Josefa Lerena Traibel is a
# FAMILYSEARCH TREE ATTACHMENT, which is SECONDARY and is exactly the kind of claim this archive
# refuses to build on.
# *** WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, unchanged: her marriage act. *** It would name her husband, her parents
# and her age in one line. Until then the census entry is NOT evidence of a Lerena-Lerena marriage,
# and this archive should stop saying that it might be.
